approach: Added simple_cycles(G, length_bound=None, *, min_length=0), inclusive lower and upper bounds; reject negative lower bounds and return no cycles for empty intervals.
Gate loops, undirected parallel-edge digons and cycle emission; retain all closure-success, unblocking and lock-relaxation operations even for short cycles.
Prune initial and subsequent SCCs/BCCs smaller than the requested minimum, following the disclosed public proposal.

For directed min_length > 3, enumerate independently in copies of qualifying biconnected blocks of the underlying undirected graph, then apply normal directed SCC partitioning. Cycles cannot cross articulation points; copies preserve shared articulation nodes between blocks. For small constant minima avoid extra block preprocessing.
Normalize the remaining lower bound to zero when every remaining nonloop/nondigon cycle qualifies, preserving the existing hot search path with a cheap emission predicate.

limitations: No claim of a universal lower-bound complexity improvement or representative production benefit.
Dense adjacency scans decrease only about 1.4%; output gating alone is not search pruning.
Extra directed block preprocessing and block copies may cost more on some graphs; final control slowdown and 1.25x geometric-mean speedup thresholds remain unmeasured.
No concurrent wall-clock comparisons or final benchmark feedback used.
